sections.h2: Which Springfield offices touch a Washington County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three desks in Springfield split the work. The PVA (Property Valuation Administrator) puts a value on every parcel. The Sheriff takes money from October until April 15. After that date the County Clerk holds whatever is still open. Nobody at the PVA's counter can accept a payment or change a rate.

Numbers printed on the Sheriff's tax page: 859-336-5420 for the PVA (acreage, assessment, wrong name or address on a bill), 859-336-5400 for the Sheriff (payments, missing bills), and 859-336-5425 for the Clerk (payoff on a prior-year delinquency). Mail and drop-box payments go to 124 East Main Street, Springfield, KY 40069, as the Sheriff's own page explains.

The bill follows the person listed in PVA records, normally the owner on January 1. If you bought or sold during the year and a bill lands with the wrong household, call the PVA or Sheriff quickly so it gets rerouted.

sections.h2: What dates and discounts apply to a Washington County bill?
sections.html:
The Sheriff cannot take a payment until the bills come over from the Clerk, which happens somewhere between October 1 and mid-October. Plan on a bill in hand around the 15th. Each bill prints four due dates, each with its own dollar amount, and the statute behind them is KRS 134.015.

What a Washington County owner pays, by when the Sheriff receives the money
ReceivedOwed
Through November 1Bill minus 2 percent
November 2 through year endPrinted amount
All of JanuaryPrinted amount plus 5 percent
February 1 through April 15Printed amount plus 10 percent

When state mailing slips, Revenue can substitute a schedule counted from the mailing date.

sections.h2: Can I use a card, or pay online, in Washington County?
sections.html:
No to both. The office explains that card fees would be handed down to taxpayers, so it declines cards, and it runs no web payment system. What it does take is simple.

  • A check or money order made out to the Washington County Sheriff's Office. Cash is fine across the counter only.
  • The yellow postcard stub from your bill, included with any mailed payment, even when one envelope covers several parcels.
  • A stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want a mailed receipt. Walk-in payers get a receipt on the spot.
  • The outdoor drop box, available after hours.

Postmarks count: an envelope stamped by the due date is honored. Partial payments get mailed back, so a seller cannot park half a bill with the Sheriff and expect the account to clear.

sections.h2: How can a Washington County owner question an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a sit-down at the PVA, then use the clerk's counter for the formal appeal. The roll sits open for public viewing for 13 days from the first Monday in May, and the written appeal is due at the end of the workday after viewing closes. A local board of assessment appeals then meets, typically a month later.

  • Bring paper: building and land descriptions, insurance policies, what construction cost, recent listings.
  • Show up. Filing without attending the hearing ends the right to go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.
  • Hire help only if the person qualifies under Kentucky's representative list, which includes attorneys, CPAs, and licensed appraisers.

If a final value lands above your claim after bills were printed, you receive a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for homestead relief in Washington County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or who are totally disabled, and who live in the home they own. The Revenue Department set the exemption at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 years. Washington County's disability route asks for the Social Security notice of award, shown at the PVA office.

Run it on the county's Census median value of $179,200. The taxable base becomes $130,100. With the state's 10.6 cents per $100 for 2025 (it was 10.9 cents in 2024), the state slice falls from about $189.95 to about $137.91. County, school, and special district rates sit on top, and the PVA can total them for any parcel.

File at the PVA with a birth certificate, driver's license, or passport. Sellers should report the sale to the PVA so the exemption comes off the old address.

sections.h2: What if taxes are still open when a Washington County house sells?
sections.html:
They travel with the land. Kentucky treats the bill as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and the delinquency lien stays attached for 11 years under KRS 134.420. Closing agents pull it up in the title search, so call the Sheriff for the current-year status and the Clerk for older years before you sign a contract.

At the April 15 handoff the Clerk records a lien, adds 10 percent plus the Sheriff's fee, and starts 1 percent monthly interest. County attorney notices go out. A tax sale may be held 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and whoever buys the certificate can add costs.

For the year of sale, a Washington County closing usually has the seller pay a pro-rated slice for months owned, with the buyer picking up the full bill later. The settlement statement shows the arrangement.

sections.h2: Why is Washington County, Kentucky different from nearby counties?
sections.html:
Carved from Nelson County in 1792, Washington County was the first county Kentucky created as a state. Springfield is the seat, joined by Mackville and Willisburg. Its 1816 courthouse is the oldest in continuous use in Kentucky, and Wikipedia notes that the center of population of Kentucky lies in the county, in Willisburg. The county voted wet in November 2024, ending its status as a dry county with one wet city.

Washington County Schools has five schools, from North Washington Elementary in Willisburg to the high school in Springfield. The county touches Anderson, Mercer, Boyle, Marion, and Nelson counties and runs on Eastern time.

  • 12,368 residents in 2025, up 2.8 percent over 2020; 20.7 percent are 65 or older.
  • 5,325 housing units for 4,852 households, averaging 2.43 people.
  • Home ownership 77.6 percent; median value $179,200; median monthly owner cost with a mortgage $1,122.
  • Median household income $61,616; per capita income $32,046; 14.1 percent poverty.
  • 19.6 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree; 22.4 minutes is the mean commute.

The county issued 26 building permits in 2025, so a seller competes mostly with other resales. An older farmhouse, a house needing repairs, or a parcel with a bill sitting at the Clerk can sell as-is for cash, with the tax cleared at closing.

faqs.q: When will my Washington County tax bill arrive?
faqs.a: Expect it around October 15. The Sheriff gets the bills from the Clerk in early to mid October and cannot accept payment before that. If nothing shows up within 10 days of mailing, call the Sheriff for a duplicate.

faqs.q: Does the Washington County Sheriff take credit cards?
faqs.a: No. Payment is by check, money order, or cash in person, and there is no online option, because card fees would be passed to taxpayers.

faqs.q: Whom do I call for prior-year Washington County taxes?
faqs.a: The County Clerk at 859-336-5425 gives payoff amounts for earlier years. Unpaid bills reach the Clerk after April 15 with added penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Do buyer or seller owe the year's tax after a mid-year sale in Washington County?
faqs.a: The contract decides, though a common pattern is a pro-rated seller share at closing and the buyer paying the full bill when it comes. Read the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Is there a senior tax break in Washington County?
faqs.a: Yes, a $49,100 homestead exemption for 2025 and 2026 for owner-occupants 65 or older or totally disabled. Apply at the PVA, 859-336-5420.
